correctness.rationale: For n=2^m and fixed numeric binary evaluation order, the cyclic transition count is twice a sum of independent prefix parity bits with weights {1,1,2,4,...,2^{m-2}}. Hence every k in (1,n/2) has exactly two coefficient vectors and two constants each, and a nonconstant word’s zero runs are only s or 2s long, whose multiplicities follow from k and the zero-balance constraint. Each length-r run contributes (r-b+1)_+ zero windows, yielding exact omega_{m,b}(k), its dyadic threshold K=max 2^j with Kb<=n and fourfold multiplicities of every subfull weight. At b=1 the Hamming law is separate; b=n saturates. Independent enumeration of all affine words and every window for m=2..6 confirms, while the all-m proof rests on binary carries and splitting, not finite testing.

originality.rationale: An October 13 and independent November 8 Resultary paper already prove the exact binary symbol-pair b=2 enumerator and pair-generation profile. The assessed novelty is strictly the all-b (especially b>=3) zero-run classification and full enumerators; these are not consequences of a single b=2 weight since longer zero-window behavior is not fixed by pair weight for arbitrary words. Pan–Ling–Liu prove minima only, Ma–Luo use different simplex coordinate ordering, Vega coprime-length cyclic codes, and Zhu–Shi Kasami codes.
